title: The Air War Over Ukraine and Russia
gist: A podcast episode note (The Russia Contingency) previewing a conversation between Michael Kofman and RUSI's Justin Bronk on the evolving airpower dynamics of the Russo-Ukrainian War, covering long-range strike campaigns, aircraft capabilities and limitations on both sides, Ukraine's difficulties employing its air assets, and air defense lessons with caution against over-extrapolating to other conflicts.

insights.claim: Justin Bronk of RUSI and Michael Kofman discuss both Russia's and Ukraine's long-range strike campaigns and the range of aircraft involved, alongside the specific capabilities and limitations each side faces in employing its air assets.
insights.speaker: War on the Rocks
insights.so_what: Signals continued analytical focus on long-range strike and airpower asymmetries as a key axis of the war, relevant to tracking demand for air-defense and strike-capable systems from both belligerents.
insights.quote: They discuss both sides’ long-range strike campaigns and the range of aircraft involved, then dig into the capabilities and limitations on each side

insights.claim: The episode explicitly cautions against extrapolating air-defense lessons from the Russo-Ukrainian War to other, different conflicts.
insights.speaker: War on the Rocks
insights.so_what: A direct warning against over-generalizing Ukraine-specific air-defense lessons (e.g., to a Taiwan or NATO-Russia scenario) — a useful check on defense analysts and planners using this war as a universal template.
insights.quote: They close with a discussion of air defense, including cautionary notes on extrapolating lessons from this war to other conflicts.
